content.key_idea: The testbed emulates EDM's compute node, memory node and switch on three separate FPGAs connected by real Ethernet links, with each node's Network Interface exposing the memory bus (AXI4) to its local application or DDR4 controller.
content.reading_order: Left-to-right across Compute Node, Switch, and Memory Node boxes, following the orange Ethernet SerDes links at the bottom that join their ports.

such as an AXI4 bus (used in our prototype (Figure 4))

summary: Figure 4 shows EDM's FPGA-based testbed setup used for evaluation. Three FPGA boards play the roles of Compute Node, Switch, and Memory Node. The Compute Node runs an Application over an AXI4 bus connected to a Network Interface with EDM-enabled Ethernet PHY ports (P0, P1); the Memory Node mirrors this with a DDR4 controller in place of the application. The Switch FPGA hosts the EDM Scheduler and forwards traffic between its two ports. Orange arrows and Ethernet SerDes labels trace the physical cabling connecting each node's ports to the switch's ports, illustrating how two EDM FPGAs and an EDM FPGA switch are wired together to emulate a real compute-memory disaggregated link for latency measurements.
summary_zh: 图4展示 EDM 的 FPGA 测试床：计算节点与内存节点各用一块 FPGA，通过 AXI4 总线连接应用/DDR4 控制器与带 EDM 逻辑的以太网 PHY 网络接口，二者经以太网 SerDes 与另一块交换机 FPGA 的端口相连。
